setting up 
```{r}
# ---- libraries (once) ----
library(tidyverse)      # dplyr, ggplot2, stringr, tidyr
library(phyloseq); library(vegan); library(microbiome); library(microViz)
library(car); library(ggpubr); library(cowplot); library(viridis); library(ape)
library(pairwiseAdonis); library(ANCOMBC)
set.seed(123)

# ---- read + subset to Summer ----
ps.cleaner <- readRDS("CH4_ps.cleaner.RDS")
ps.cleaner.filtered <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps.cleaner) > 0, ps.cleaner)

dist.sum.git.ps <- subset_samples(ps.cleaner.filtered, Experiment == "Summer")
dist.sum.git.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(dist.sum.git.ps) > 0, dist.sum.git.ps)

# ---- clean once, at the all-weeks level ----
tt <- tax_table(dist.sum.git.ps); colnames(tt)[7] <- "Sequence"
tax_table(dist.sum.git.ps) <- tt

sd <- data.frame(sample_data(dist.sum.git.ps))
sd$is.neg <- NULL
sd$Temperature <- factor(sd$Temperature, levels = c(22, 26))
sd$Treatment   <- factor(sd$Treatment,
                         levels = c("ND","Few Small","Many Small","Few Large","HD"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sd$Temperature), !anyNA(sd$Treatment))   # stops if any label was lost
sample_data(dist.sum.git.ps) <- sample_data(sd)

# ---- Week 5 objects ----
dist.sum.git.wk5.ps <- subset_samples(dist.sum.git.ps, Week == 5)
dist.sum.git.wk5.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps) > 0, dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)

dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps <- subset_samples(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps, Treatment != "HD")
dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps) > 0,
                                       dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps)
sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps) <-
  sample_data(droplevels(data.frame(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps))))

# ---- verify (should match what you saw before) ----
stopifnot(nsamples(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps) == 27, ntaxa(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps) == 13467,
          nsamples(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps) == 24)
rank_names(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)    # 7th = "Sequence"
table(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps)$Temperature,
      sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps)$Treatment)   # 3 per cell
```

```{r}
ps  <- dist.sum.git.wk5.ps
otu <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")                      # samples x ASVs
seqs <- as.character(tax_table(ps)[, "Sequence"])

## 1. IDs and sequences are consistent
anyDuplicated(taxa_names(ps))                           # 0
anyDuplicated(seqs)                                     # 0
all(grepl("^[ACGT]+$", seqs))                           # TRUE (no N or odd characters)
table(nchar(seqs))                                      # most should be ~252-254 bp
sum(otu[, nchar(seqs) < 250 | nchar(seqs) > 256]) / sum(otu) * 100   # % of reads in off-length ASVs

## 2. Sparsity and prevalence (this informs the prevalence filter)
mean(otu == 0) * 100                                    # % of zero cells
prev  <- colSums(otu > 0)
reads <- colSums(otu)
data.frame(
  prevalence = c("1 sample", "2 samples", "3-5 samples", "6+ samples"),
  n_ASVs     = c(sum(prev == 1), sum(prev == 2), sum(prev %in% 3:5), sum(prev >= 6)),
  pct_reads  = c(sum(reads[prev == 1]), sum(reads[prev == 2]),
                 sum(reads[prev %in% 3:5]), sum(reads[prev >= 6])) / sum(reads) * 100
)

## 3. Dominant ASVs
top <- sort(reads, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
data.frame(ASV = names(top), pct_reads = round(top / sum(reads) * 100, 2),
           as.data.frame(as(tax_table(ps)[names(top), c("Phylum","Class","Genus")], "matrix")))

## 4. Richness vs. depth (relevant to the rarefaction decision)
cor(rowSums(otu > 0), rowSums(otu), method = "spearman")

## 5. Read-weighted taxonomy assignment (the check from before)
tt <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps))
sapply(c("Phylum","Class","Order","Family","Genus"),
       function(r) sum(reads[!is.na(tt[[r]])]) / sum(reads) * 100)

## 6. Do the saved pipeline files match the phyloseq object?
seqtab.orig <- readRDS("seqtab.nochim_ch4_16S.rds")
rownames(seqtab.orig) <- gsub("F|R", "", rownames(seqtab.orig))        # same cleanup you used
rownames(seqtab.orig) <- gsub("_filt.fastq.gz", "", rownames(seqtab.orig))
common_s <- intersect(rownames(otu), rownames(seqtab.orig))
length(common_s)                                        # 27
all(seqs %in% colnames(seqtab.orig))                    # TRUE
m <- otu; colnames(m) <- seqs
all(m[common_s, seqs] == seqtab.orig[common_s, seqs])   # TRUE: counts unchanged
anyDuplicated(sample_names(ps.cleaner))                 # 0 across all 3 experiments

#looking at taxonomic resolution
reads <- taxa_sums(ps)
sapply(c("Phylum","Class","Order","Family","Genus"), function(r) {
  x  <- tt[[r]]
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !grepl("uncultured|unclassified|Incertae|metagenome", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  sum(reads[ok]) / sum(reads) * 100
})
```

- Filter?: requiring presence in at least 3 samples (matching your replicate number) drops 7,526 ASVs but only 5.4% of reads.

- note: Don’t apply this filter before alpha diversity, since rare ASVs contribute to richness.

BARPLOT
~

```{r}
make_tax_plot_wk5 <- function(ps, tax_rank, rare_cutoff = 1) {
  # 1. Subset Week 5 samples
  ps_wk5 <- subset_samples(ps, Week == 5)
  ps_wk5 <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_wk5) > 0, ps_wk5)
  # 2. Aggregate ASVs at selected taxonomic level
  ps_tax <- tax_glom(ps_wk5, taxrank = tax_rank, NArm = FALSE)
  # 3. Relative abundance within each sample
  ps_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_tax, function(x) x / sum(x))
  # 4. Convert to dataframe
  summer_df <- psmelt(ps_rel)
  summer_df$Taxon <- as.character(summer_df[[tax_rank]])
  #max group mean
    taxon_overall <- summer_df %>%
    group_by(Sample, Temperature, Treatment, Taxon) %>%
    summarise(Ab = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(Temperature, Treatment, Taxon) %>%
    summarise(Group_Mean = mean(Ab) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
    group_by(Taxon) %>%
    summarise(Mean_Percentage = max(Group_Mean), .groups = "drop")
  
  # 6. Group unassigned and rare taxa
  summer_df <- summer_df %>%
    left_join(taxon_overall, by = "Taxon") %>%
    mutate(
      Taxon_grouped = case_when(
        is.na(Taxon) | trimws(Taxon) == "" |
          tolower(trimws(Taxon)) %in% c("na", "unclassified", "unknown") ~
          paste("Unassigned at", tax_rank, "level"),
        Mean_Percentage < rare_cutoff ~ "Rare taxa",
        TRUE ~ Taxon
      )
    )
  # 7. Combine taxa within each sample
  summer_sample_df <- summer_df %>%
    group_by(Sample, Temperature, Treatment, Taxon_grouped) %>%
    summarise(Relative_Abundance = sum(Abundance), .groups = "drop")
  # 8. Average across biological replicates
  summer_summary <- summer_sample_df %>%
    group_by(Temperature, Treatment, Taxon_grouped) %>%
    summarise(Mean_Relative_Abundance = mean(Relative_Abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
      Temperature = factor(Temperature, levels = c("22", "26")),
      Treatment = factor(Treatment,
                         levels = c("ND", "Few Small", "Many Small", "Few Large", "HD")),
      Mean_Percentage = Mean_Relative_Abundance * 100
    )
  # 9. Set up colors
  taxon_levels <- unique(as.character(summer_summary$Taxon_grouped))
  distinct_palette <- c(
    "#1f78b4", "#FF69B4", "#33a02c", "#ff7f00", "#984ea3", "#e41a1c",
    "#4ea3d9", "#b07cc6", "#66c2a5", "#a65628", "#f781bf", "#238b45",
    "#6a3d9a", "#e6ab02", "#00a6d6", "#d95f02", "#8c6bb1", "#41ae76",
    "#fb6a4a", "#377eb8", "#cab2d6", "#b15928", "#74c476", "#e7298a",
    "#ffd92f", "#006d2c", "#a6cee3", "#d4b9da", "#ff9933", "#7b3294"
  )
  special_colors <- c("Rare taxa" = "grey70")
  special_colors[paste("Unassigned at", tax_rank, "level")] <- "darkblue"

  regular_taxa <- setdiff(taxon_levels, names(special_colors))

  # FIXED: warn if colors will repeat
  if (length(regular_taxa) > length(distinct_palette)) {
    message(length(regular_taxa), " taxa but only ", length(distinct_palette),
            " colors: colors will repeat. Consider rare_cutoff > 0.")
  }
  regular_colors <- setNames(
    rep(distinct_palette, length.out = length(regular_taxa)),
    regular_taxa
  )
  taxon_colors <- c(regular_colors, special_colors)
  # 10. Create bar plot
  summer_plot <- ggplot(
    summer_summary,
    aes(x = Temperature, y = Mean_Percentage, fill = Taxon_grouped)
  ) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    facet_wrap(~ Treatment, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = taxon_colors, breaks = taxon_levels, drop = FALSE) +
    # FIXED: scale_y has no limits; coord_cartesian sets the range safely
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(
      x = "Temperature (°C)",
      y = "Mean Relative Abundance (%)",
      fill = tax_rank,
      title = paste("Week 5 Summer Microbial Community:", tax_rank)
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.4, "cm"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    )
  list(
    aggregated = ps_tax,
    dataframe = summer_df,
    sample_summary = summer_sample_df,
    summary = summer_summary,
    colors = taxon_colors,
    plot = summer_plot
  )
}
```

stacking and matching colors
```{r}
library(cowplot)

unassigned <- "Unassigned at Class level"

# taxa in each plot (keeps each plot's own legend order)
rare.levels <- unique(as.character(class.rare$summary$Taxon_grouped))
all.levels  <- unique(as.character(class.all$summary$Taxon_grouped))

# common Classes first, so they get unique colors
common <- setdiff(rare.levels, c("Rare taxa", unassigned))
others <- setdiff(all.levels, c(common, "Rare taxa", unassigned))

# your 30-color palette, taken from the function's output
pal <- unique(unname(class.all$colors[!names(class.all$colors) %in% c("Rare taxa", unassigned)]))

shared.colors <- c(
  setNames(rep(pal, length.out = length(c(common, others))), c(common, others)),
  "Rare taxa" = "grey70"
)
shared.colors[unassigned] <- "darkblue"

class.all.matched <- class.all$plot +
  scale_fill_manual(values = shared.colors, breaks = all.levels) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +          # 1 = one long column, 2–3 = more compact
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"))
class.rare.matched <- class.rare$plot +
  scale_fill_manual(values = shared.colors, breaks = rare.levels) +
  theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"))

class.stack <- plot_grid(
  class.rare.matched, class.all.matched,
  ncol = 1, labels = c("A", "B"), label_size = 14,
  align = "v", axis = "lr",
  rel_heights = c(1, 1.6)                          # gives the bottom panel extra height for the taller legend
)
```

above code interpretation 
How the plots are built
- For each sample, read counts at the chosen rank (Phylum or Class) become relative abundance. The denominator is all reads in that sample, including unassigned ones.
- Taxa are summed within each sample first. This is the step that fixes the bars not reaching 100%.
- The 3 replicates in each Temperature × Treatment group are then averaged equally, regardless of sequencing depth.
- HD appears only at 22°C because it has no 26°C samples.
- What “Rare taxa” means (max group mean version)
- A taxon goes in the Rare bin if its mean relative abundance is below 1% in every Temperature × Treatment group (rare_cutoff = 1). Put another way, its highest group mean is under 1%.
- Each group mean is the average of that group’s 3 replicates. HD at 22°C counts as its own group, so there are 9 groups.
- A taxon that reaches 1% or more in at least one group stays visible, even if it is near zero everywhere else. This keeps treatment-specific taxa in the figure.
- It is still a group-mean rule, not a per-sample rule. A taxon that is high in a single replicate but averages under 1% in its group is still binned.
- Every taxon shown separately is at least 1% in at least one bar. The Rare bin can still add up to a noticeable share of some groups, so report that share.
- “Rare” refers to low-abundance taxa at that rank, not rare ASVs.
- Unassigned reads form their own category and are not counted as rare.
- rare_cutoff = 0 bins nothing, which gives your all-taxa plots.
- Suggested wording for methods
“Taxa with a mean relative abundance below 1% in every experimental group are shown as ‘Rare taxa’.”


~
Repeated rarefaction = repeated subsampling to a specific sequencing depth that computes a single mean value for each sample.
Rarefying = a single subsampling to a specific sequencing depth that computes a value for each ASV for each sample.
~

RAREFACTION CURVE 
~
```{r}
#curve set up
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)

# Week 5 subset (same as in your barplot function)
ps_wk5 <- subset_samples(dist.sum.git.ps, Week == 5)
ps_wk5 <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_wk5) > 0, ps_wk5)

# OTU table: rarecurve() needs SAMPLES as rows
wk5.otu <- as(otu_table(ps_wk5), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps_wk5)) wk5.otu <- t(wk5.otu)

# metadata in the same sample order as the OTU table
wk5.metadata <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_wk5))[rownames(wk5.otu), ]

# colors by treatment
treatment_colors <- c("ND" = "#1f78b4", "Few Small" = "#FF69B4",
                      "Many Small" = "#33a02c", "Few Large" = "#ff7f00",
                      "HD" = "#984ea3")
sample_colors <- unname(treatment_colors[as.character(wk5.metadata$Treatment)])
```

```{r}
vegan::rarecurve(
  wk5.otu,
  step = 1000,
  col = sample_colors,
  lty = ifelse(wk5.metadata$Temperature == "22", 1, 2),
  lwd = 1.5,
  label = FALSE,
  xlab = "Sequencing depth (reads)",
  ylab = "Observed ASV richness",
  main = "Week 5 Summer rarefaction curves"
)
```

Rarefying = a single subsampling to a specific sequencing depth that computes a value for each ASV for each sample.

```{r}
  trimOTUs = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

Rarefaction = repeated subsampling to a specific sequencing depth that computes a single mean value for each sample @ lowest depth 
```{r}
#LOOP
otu <- as(otu_table(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)) otu <- t(otu)      # samples x ASVs

n_iter <- 100
set.seed(123)

sum_counts <- matrix(0, nrow(otu), ncol(otu), dimnames = dimnames(otu))
alpha_arr  <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(nrow(otu), 3, n_iter),
                    dimnames = list(rownames(otu),
                                    c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"), NULL))

for (i in seq_len(n_iter)) {
  r <- suppressWarnings(vegan::rrarefy(otu, sample = 38255))   # one rarefied draw
  sum_counts <- sum_counts + r
  alpha_arr[, "Observed",   i] <- rowSums(r > 0)
  alpha_arr[, "Shannon",    i] <- vegan::diversity(r, "shannon")
  alpha_arr[, "InvSimpson", i] <- vegan::diversity(r, "invsimpson")
}

# 1. averaged alpha table (one row per sample)
alpha_rare1_avg <- as.data.frame(apply(alpha_arr, c(1, 2), mean))

# 2. averaged-count phyloseq object (plots and descriptive summaries only)
mean_counts <- sum_counts / n_iter
rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps <- phyloseq(
  otu_table(mean_counts, taxa_are_rows = FALSE),
  sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps),
  tax_table(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)
)
rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps <- prune_taxa(
  taxa_sums(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps) > 0, rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)

#SAMPLE CHECK
nsamples(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)
summary(sample_sums(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps))
ntaxa(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)
```

Making alpha dataframes for unrare and single rare  + adding in metadata
```{r}
make_alpha_df <- function(ps) {
  alpha <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "InvSimpson"))
  alpha$Sample      <- rownames(alpha)
  md                <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))
  alpha$Treatment   <- md[alpha$Sample, "Treatment"]
  alpha$Temperature <- md[alpha$Sample, "Temperature"]
  alpha$Depth       <- as.numeric(sample_sums(ps)[alpha$Sample])
  alpha$Evenness    <- ifelse(alpha$Observed > 1, alpha$Shannon / log(alpha$Observed), NA)
  alpha[, c("Sample","Treatment","Temperature","Depth",
            "Observed","Shannon","InvSimpson","Evenness")]
}

# 1. unrarefied
alpha_unrare <- make_alpha_df(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)
# 2. single-draw rarefied
alpha_rare_single <- make_alpha_df(rare.dist.sum.git.wk5.ps)
# 3. averaged over 100 draws (reshape your loop output to match)
md <- data.frame(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.ps))
alpha_rare_avg <- alpha_rare1_avg
alpha_rare_avg$Sample      <- rownames(alpha_rare_avg)
alpha_rare_avg$Treatment   <- md[alpha_rare_avg$Sample, "Treatment"]
alpha_rare_avg$Temperature <- md[alpha_rare_avg$Sample, "Temperature"]
alpha_rare_avg$Depth       <- 38255
alpha_rare_avg$Evenness    <- ifelse(alpha_rare_avg$Observed > 1,
                                     alpha_rare_avg$Shannon / log(alpha_rare_avg$Observed), NA)
alpha_rare_avg <- alpha_rare_avg[, names(alpha_unrare)]    # same column order

alpha_sets <- l255ist(unrarefied = alpha_unrare,
                   rare_avg   = alpha_rare_avg,
                   rare_single = alpha_rare_single)
```

models! 2 way anovas unrare data

- models passed assumptions

```{r}
# Two-way ANOVA
anova.unrare <- aov(
  Evenness ~ Treatment * Temperature,
  data = alpha_unrare_noHD
)
summary(anova.unrare)
# Assumption checks
qqnorm(residuals(anova.unrare))
qqline(residuals(anova.unrare), col = "red")
shapiro.test(residuals(anova.unrare))
leveneTest(
  Evenness ~ Treatment * Temperature,
  data = alpha_unrare_noHD
)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(anova.unrare, which = 1)   # residuals vs fitted: look for a funnel shape
plot(anova.unrare, which = 2)   # Q-Q plot
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

#effect sizes. A p-value alone says little with n=3 per cell. This adds the share of variance each term explains:
tab <- summary(anova.unrare)[[1]]
tab$eta_sq <- round(tab$`Sum Sq` / sum(tab$`Sum Sq`), 3)
tab
```

CONCLUSIONS FROM ALPHA 
Alpha diversity (Observed richness, Shannon, inverse Simpson, and Pielou’s evenness)
- rarefied to 38,255 reads
- rarefaction 100 times to 38,255 
- unrare data 
- no difference!
- Alpha Diversity did not differ delectably among disturbance treatments or between temperatures, and there was no Treatment × Temperature interaction (all p > 0.05; n = 3 per group)

BETA DIVERISTY
~~

Type of Data & Filter Compared Here 
1	Unrarefied, no HD (24 mats) - 	ASVs present in at least 3 mats
2	Unrarefied, no HD (24 mats)	 - purgeOutliers ASV rules (otu.cut 0.0001, zero.cut 0.02), sample step off (sampleZcut = -100)
3	Rarefied (100-draw average, 38,255 reads), no HD - 	No filter

*All three use CLR with a pseudocount of 1, then Euclidean distance (Aitchison).

```{r}
              destfile = file.path(tmp, "MCMC.OTU.tar.gz"), mode = "wb")
```

```{r}
## --- same set-up as your original script, built from your Week 5 no-HD object ---
ps <- dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps
seqtab.cleanest <- as(otu_table(ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(ps)) seqtab.cleanest <- t(seqtab.cleanest)
seqtab.cleanest <- as.data.frame(seqtab.cleanest)            # samples x ASVs

nums    <- 1:nrow(seqtab.cleanest)
samples <- rownames(seqtab.cleanest)
int         <- cbind(sample = 0, seqtab.cleanest)
seq.formcmc <- cbind(X = 0, int)
seq.formcmc$X      <- nums
seq.formcmc$sample <- samples
dim(seq.formcmc)

## --- trim underrepresented ASVs (same call as your original) ---
seq.trim.allinfo <- purgeOutliers(seq.formcmc,
                                  count.columns = 3:ncol(seq.formcmc),   # replaces your hard-coded 3:10011
                                  sampleZcut = -100,                     # set to -100 to keep all 24 mats
                                  otu.cut = 0.0001, zero.cut = 0.02)
dim(seq.trim.allinfo)

seq.trim <- seq.trim.allinfo[, 3:ncol(seq.trim.allinfo)]    # replaces your hard-coded 3:1685
rownames(seq.trim) <- seq.trim.allinfo$sample               # keeps the sample names
write.csv(seq.trim, file = "seqtab.trim.csv")
seq.trim <- read.csv("seqtab.trim.csv", row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)

## --- what was removed? ---
removed.samples <- setdiff(samples, rownames(seq.trim))
removed.samples                                              # which mat(s), if any
ncol(seq.trim)                                               # ASVs kept
sum(seq.trim) / sum(seqtab.cleanest[rownames(seq.trim), ]) * 100    # % of reads kept (in the retained mats)

## --- back into phyloseq ---
dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps <- prune_taxa(colnames(seq.trim), ps)
dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps <- prune_samples(rownames(seq.trim), dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps)
sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps) <-
  sample_data(droplevels(data.frame(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps))))

ntaxa(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps); nsamples(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps)
table(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps)$Temperature,
      sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.purged.ps)$Treatment)
```
- ASVs were filtered following the MCMC.OTU purgeOutliers rules: ASVs with under 0.01% of total reads, or detected in under 2% of samples, were removed. The function’s sample-level outlier rule (log total counts, z < −2.5) was not applied, to retain all replicates (also read depth for lowest depth sample is fine)

Differences between 2 filters:
- FILTER prevalence filter removes ASVs found in only 1 or 2 mats (about 56% of your ASVs) whatever their read count
- PURGED purgeOutliers removes ASVs with under roughly 250 total reads (probably over three-quarters of them), even if they appear in many mats, and its 2% prevalence rule does almost nothing with 24 mats.

```{r}
# Extract ASV table (samples as rows)
wk5.noHD.seqtab <- as(otu_table(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.filt.ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.filt.ps)) {
  wk5.noHD.seqtab <- t(wk5.noHD.seqtab)
}

#CLR transformation done by hand (pseudocount of 1 added before the log)
wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab <- log(wk5.noHD.seqtab + 1)
wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab <- wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab - rowMeans(wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab)

# Calculate Euclidean distances on the CLR table ( Aitchison distance)
wk5.noHD.dist <- vegdist(wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab, method = "euclidean")

# Extract metadata
wk5.noHD.samdf <- data.frame(sample_data(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.filt.ps))

# Check sample alignment
identical(rownames(wk5.noHD.samdf), labels(wk5.noHD.dist))
```

```{r}
wk5.noHD.rare.avg.dist <- vegdist(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.clr.seqtab, method = "euclidean")

# Extract metadata
wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf <- data.frame(sample_data(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps))

# Check sample alignment
identical(rownames(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf), labels(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.dist))
nsamples(rare.avg.dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.ps)     # should be 24
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Beta dispersion by Treatment
rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.treatment <- betadisper(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.dist, wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Treatment, bias.adjust = TRUE)
anova(rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.treatment)
permutest(rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.treatment, pairwise = TRUE, permutations = 9999)

# Beta dispersion by Temperature
rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.temperature <- betadisper(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.dist, wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Temperature, bias.adjust = TRUE)
anova(rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.temperature)
permutest(rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.temperature, pairwise = TRUE, permutations = 9999)

#beta dispersion across all 8 Treatment x Temperature groups
wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Group <- interaction(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Treatment, wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Temperature, bias.adjust = TRUE)
rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.group <- betadisper(wk5.noHD.rare.avg.dist, wk5.noHD.rare.avg.samdf$Group)
permutest(rare.wk5.noHD.betadisper.group, permutations = 9999)
```

Temperature  1     8516 0.06088 1.4364 0.0382 *

Analysis	Temperature R²	p
(1) CLR, prevalence ≥ 3, unrarefied	  0.062	0.049*

~
Beta diversity results summary
~
*The effect size doesn’t change. R² is 0.06 to 0.07 in every analysis
*Temperature explains about 6 to 7% of community variation however you filter or normalize.
*Primary: (1), prevalence-filtered, unrarefied - filter rule is easy to justify. 

*Temperature explained about 6% of the variation in community composition (PERMANOVA on CLR-transformed ASV abundances, R² = 0.062, p = 0.049). Results were similar across filtering and normalization choices (R² = 0.060–0.069; p = 0.027–0.055m indicating a small and borderline effect. Disturbance treatment and the Treatment × Temperature interaction were not supported

PCOA PLOTS
~
```{r}
library(ggplot2); library(cowplot); library(ggrepel)


# ---------- PCoA of the prevalence-filtered CLR/Euclidean distances (set 1) ----------
stopifnot(ncol(wk5.noHD.clr.seqtab) == ntaxa(dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.filt.ps))   # confirms this is the filtered set
stopifnot(identical(rownames(wk5.noHD.samdf), labels(wk5.noHD.dist)))

wk5.noHD.pcoa <- ape::pcoa(wk5.noHD.dist)
wk5.noHD.pcoa.percent <- round(wk5.noHD.pcoa$values$Relative_eig * 100, 1)
wk5.noHD.pcoa.df <- cbind(
  data.frame(PCoA1 = wk5.noHD.pcoa$vectors[, 1],
             PCoA2 = wk5.noHD.pcoa$vectors[, 2]),
  wk5.noHD.samdf
)

# shared look for both panels
temp_cols  <- c("22" = "blue3", "26" = "red3")
base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))

xlab <- paste0("PCoA 1 (", wk5.noHD.pcoa.percent[1], "%)")
ylab <- paste0("PCoA 2 (", wk5.noHD.pcoa.percent[2], "%)")

# ---------- Panel A: ASV-level PCoA, shaded Temperature ellipses, no arrows ----------
pA <- ggplot(wk5.noHD.pcoa.df,
             aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = Temperature, shape = Treatment)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = Temperature, fill = Temperature),
               geom = "polygon", level = 0.95,
               alpha = 0.18, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(values = temp_cols) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("ND" = 16, "Few Small" = 17,
                                "Many Small" = 15, "Few Large" = 18)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = temp_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = temp_cols) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5,
           label = "Temperature: R² = 0.062, p = 0.049") +
  labs(title = "ASV profiles: CLR/Euclidean PCoA", x = xlab, y = ylab) +
  base_theme

# ---------- Class arrows (descriptive overlay only; axes stay ASV-level) ----------
cls.ps <- dist.sum.git.wk5.noHD.filt.ps

# ASV count table with samples as rows
asv <- as(otu_table(cls.ps), "matrix")
if (taxa_are_rows(cls.ps)) asv <- t(asv)

# Class name for each ASV; unassigned ASVs are pooled together
cls <- as.character(tax_table(cls.ps)[colnames(asv), "Class"])
cls[is.na(cls) | trimws(cls) == ""] <- "Unassigned"

# sum ASV counts within each Class -> samples x Classes
class.counts <- t(rowsum(t(asv), group = cls))

# match the sample order used in the PCoA
class.counts <- class.counts[rownames(wk5.noHD.samdf), ]

stopifnot(identical(rownames(class.counts), rownames(wk5.noHD.samdf)))

keep.cls  <- colSums(class.counts > 0) >= 3
clr.class <- log(class.counts[, keep.cls] + 1)
clr.class <- clr.class - rowMeans(clr.class)

# arrow = correlation of each Class's CLR abundance with the two plotted PCoA axes
# (same vectors vegan::envfit would draw); longer arrow = Class lines up better with this plane
ax   <- as.matrix(wk5.noHD.pcoa.df[, c("PCoA1", "PCoA2")])
cors <- cor(clr.class, ax)
len  <- sqrt(rowSums(cors^2))

# optional: only consider common Classes (mean relative abundance >= 1%) to avoid chance hits among rare ones
# common <- colMeans(class.counts / rowSums(class.counts)) >= 0.01
# len <- len[names(len) %in% names(common)[common]]

top  <- names(sort(len, decreasing = TRUE))[1:10]
mult <- 0.8 * min(max(abs(ax[, 1])) / max(abs(cors[top, 1])),
                  max(abs(ax[, 2])) / max(abs(cors[top, 2])))
arrow.df <- data.frame(Class = top,
                       PCoA1 = cors[top, 1] * mult,
                       PCoA2 = cors[top, 2] * mult)

# ---------- Panel B: same ASV-level PCoA + Class arrows ----------
pB <- ggplot(wk5.noHD.pcoa.df,
             aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, color = Temperature, shape = Treatment)) +
  geom_segment(data = arrow.df, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PCoA1, yend = PCoA2),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey40",
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"))) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = arrow.df, aes(x = PCoA1, y = PCoA2, label = Class),
                           inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 0, color = "grey20",
                           max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_color_manual(values = temp_cols) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(values = temp_cols) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("ND" = 16, "Few Small" = 17,
                                "Many Small" = 15, "Few Large" = 18)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = temp_cols) +
  labs(title = "Same PCoA with Class arrows (exploratory)", x = xlab, y = ylab) +
  base_theme

# ---------- Combine with cowplot, one shared legend ----------
legend <- cowplot::get_legend(pA)
panels <- cowplot::plot_grid(pA + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                             pB + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                             labels = c("A", "B"), label_size = 14, nrow = 1,
                             align = "hv", axis = "tblr")
final.fig <- cowplot::plot_grid(panels, legend, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 0.14))
final.fig

#ggsave("Week5_beta_diversity_two_panel_nolab.pdf", final.fig, width = 10, height = 5)
```

Final Thoughts
-- The data checks:  ASV table match the DADA2 output, the taxonomy and cleanup are verified, and 3 independent mats for each experimental group
- Alpha diversity was done on rarefied, rarefaction (100 subsamples) and unrarefied data (all the same results)
- Beta diversity used FILTERED, PURGED AND RAREFIED data - all data CLR transformed & euclidean distances used 
- Differential abundance uses raw counts (Temperature + Treatment)
- The results agree across approaches: alpha diversity was null in every rarefied model, and beta analyses put Temperature at about 6 to 7% of variation (slight affect), with no interaction and no sign of unequal dispersion.
- Diff abundance results ~ only 3 mats per treat x temp group & strict holm correction, no sig classes makes sense.
